sources: CCSDS 502.0-B-3 7.5.10: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[.d->d][Z] or YYYY-DDDThh:mm:ss[.d->d][Z]; all fields with leading zeros; Z optional
iso: the instant each valid string denotes, as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.ffffff' UTC; a parse_epoch hook is compared with it within 2 us (D-119)

leap seconds: the 27 dates of IERS Leap_Second.dat (https://hpiers.obspm.fr/iers/bul/bulc/Leap_Second.dat, through Bulletin C 72), the last 2016-12-31; CGPM 2026 Resolution 5 (https://www.bipm.org/en/cgpm-2026/resolution-5): continuous UTC from 20 May 2027; second 60 is valid only at 23:59:60 UTC on those dates (D-382)

valid.note: CCSDS annex G example, day-of-year form
leap second: ss = 60 permitted (7.5.10 NOTE); a datetime cannot carry second 60, so the instant one second earlier (iso) or the next midnight (iso_alternatives) is accepted
the first leap second, on a 30 June (IERS); read as the instant one second earlier or the next midnight (D-382)
a leap second in the day-of-year form, with a fraction and a Z (D-382)
day 366 of a leap year, not a leap second: the last day of 2024 in the day-of-year form (D-384)
the last second a signed 32-bit time_t holds (2**31 - 1 seconds after 1970) (D-385)
the first second past a signed 32-bit time_t: a reader through one wraps to 1901-12-13 (D-385)
well past 2038, in the day-of-year form with a fraction (D-385)
before 1970, a negative time_t: a reader through an unsigned 32-bit time_t wraps it to 2096 (D-385)

invalid.reason: TLE epoch field, not an OMM epoch
only 'Z' is permitted as time-code terminator in 7.5.10 (the XSD pattern is more permissive)
day of year 366 in a year of 365 days: 7.5.10's DDD is a day of that year
second 60 outside the last minute of a day: a leap second is only ever 23:59:60 UTC (SM-26's L1, D-382)
30 June before the first leap second (1972-06-30) (SM-26's L2, D-382)
30 June in a year whose leap second was on 31 December (1977-12-31) (D-382)
day-of-year form of 2016-06-30, not a leap-second date; 2016's was 31 December (D-382)
no leap second was announced for 31 December 2026 (IERS Bulletin C 72) (D-382)
after 20 May 2027 UTC is continuous and has no second 60 (CGPM 2026 Resolution 5) (SM-26's L2, D-382)
second 60 with a fraction and a Z outside the last minute of a day (D-382)
second 60 in another minute of a leap-second date: only 23:59:60 is the leap second (D-382)
31 December between leap seconds (1979-12-31, 1981-06-30): no leap second that day (D-382)

parser_hazard: A parser hard-coded to '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f' (for example python-sgp4's sgp4.omm.initialize) rejects thirteen of the fifteen valid strings above: every one but the two calendar forms with a fraction and no Z (measured with python-sgp4 2.27: six of eight, D-331; eight of ten, D-382; nine of eleven, D-384; thirteen of fifteen, D-385).
